desc:
A grid describes a field: 0 is an open cell, 1 is a wall and 2 is a cell that is infected at minute 0 (there is at least one).

Every minute, each open cell that shares a side (up, down, left or right) with an infected cell becomes infected; all cells that qualify in a minute change at the same moment, and walls never change. Return the number of infected cells (the initial ones included) after exactly t minutes.

grid = [[2,0,0],
        [1,1,0],
        [0,0,0]]

t = 3  -> 4      (cells (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (1,2))
t = 4  -> 5
constraints: grid[r][c] is 0, 1 or 2, and at least one cell is 2
hints: Infection moves one step per minute in all directions at once, so the minute a cell gets infected equals its distance from the nearest infected cell.
Start one BFS with all initially infected cells in the queue and process it one level (one minute) at a time.
Stop after t levels, or earlier if a level is empty. Count the initial cells plus every cell added in each processed level.
editorial: This is a multi-source BFS with a depth limit. Put all cells with value 2 into the first frontier and mark them visited. For minute 1, 2, ..., t, build the next frontier from the unvisited open neighbours of the current one, add its size to the counter and make it the current frontier. If a frontier is ever empty, nothing else can be infected and the loop stops, which also makes a huge t cheap.
Each cell enters a frontier at most once, so the running time is O(rows × cols) however large t is. Simulating minute by minute with a full scan of the grid would cost O(rows × cols) per minute.
